Since \(8\frac13\% = \frac1{12}\), Ian ate \(\frac{13}{12}\) as many pieces as Max.

If \(nm\) were even, black and white counts would be equal, impossible. So \(nm\) is odd, and the counts differ by \(1\). Since Ian ate more, \(B=W+1\).

\[
\frac{W+1}{W}=\frac{13}{12}
\]
\[
12W+12=13W \Rightarrow W=12,\quad B=13
\]
Thus total pieces:
\[
nm=25
\]
With \(m,n>1\), the only factorization is \(5\cdot 5\), so
\[
m+n=10
\]

\[
\boxed{10}
\]
